transcription: How to ride the Hello Kitty bullet train in Japan. Yup, you heard me right. Japan has its own Hello Kitty shinkansen. And riding it is actually really complicated, so you're gonna wanna watch the whole video so you don't miss anything. First, you're gonna wanna go to the JR ticket counter to get your tickets. Be sure to check the train timetable the night before. Make sure you're waiting in line for cart number two of the train, because that's the seat room with the Hello Kitty theme, and it's first come first serve. Once you've secured your seats, it's time to go to cart one. This is the Hello Kitty Plaza, where you can buy exclusive Hello Kitty shingansen goods. It also features adorable photo spots, where you can take super Kauai content. #lamp #isamunoguchi #noguchi #lamps #tokyo #interiordesign #designfurniture #homedecor #japan".
transcription: We flew all the way to Japan and on top of our bucket list was finding our dream lamp designed by world-famous Izamono Gucci and let me just tell you we were lucky. So here's the full tour of every location we checked out. First up is CB Coffee. This is not just the coffee, it's also a little retail space where they supposedly sell some lamps, but despite them hanging everywhere, this time we unfortunately struck out. But at least the coffee was great. Around the corner I discovered one of my favorite models in a little ceramic shop, so I asked the owner where she has it from. She was so kind to write it down so we checked it out the next day. Which was unfortunately a little bit rainy but this doesn't stop us. Or does it because the first stop being a museum was closed. Little bummer but at least you get the hint from the lady. Which is Skins Are Raisin. This is a luxury mall offering interior items on their top floor. And while already celebrating single lamps, our excitement got stopped immediately because the staff told us there's a waiting list for over 10 months. So as you can see on my face, I needed to get cheered up. And in order to do so, we went to the supposedly best coffee in Tokyo. And if it actually lives up to its hype, I will let you know my next week. And after enjoying my coffee, we went to one of your biggest recommendations, which is Ozeki Gallery. This space is dedicated to showcasing his Amonoguchi's work, which is incredible. They literally have every lamp ever produced by him, and although being mesmerized by all the beautiful lighting, they unfortunately just had one particular lamp in stock. The biggest one I'm not able to carry home. But we were not defeated just yet, because there are still two shops left on our list. And the opposite is because we got the hint that Hermel Miller is usually the first one to receive new stock. And oh boy, she was right. This dev showed us not just one but three different models. And since we couldn't decide, we just bought them all. And if you're wondering why just not buy them in Germany, you're essentially getting free for the price of one year. And on top of that, I will always remember them as our Japan lamps, which makes them that more special. Our last stop was the second term emela, which was even bigger. And although they didn't have the lamps we were looking for, they had some Akari posters I've never seen before. And yes, these are the exact same prints you can usually find on the lamps. And since they even made from the same rice paper material, we had to get them. I am beyond stoked how they look in our space. So let me know what you think and follow for part 2 when we hang up our new precious fines.
